checks.detail: CPRPlacedSourceEventPlan replays the preserved native tempo for Start and preserved scalar type10 for Length/Offset. Only the explicit mode supplies project.sampleRate to existing builder and reader arithmetic. CPRNativeTimelineStream keeps each retained accessor sourceRate→sourceRate, while its output format uses timelineRate. There is no SRC insertion or source-rate rewrite in this path.

App uses positive integral rate and factor1, making the concrete widened Float32 base product equal the supplied rate. This does not establish that the native registry config, VstDeck global period or device has those values. BRP2/BRP5 preserve that distinction.

Before preparation and again in stream construction, separately quantized start/end/offset must yield last>first, seek>=0, and last-first<=availableFrames-seek. Up-clock raw windows exceeding actual source are rejected; no repetition, interpolation or EOF padding is used. The previous native selector/zero-length-intersection/positive full-read rules remain unchanged.

A saved native offset expressed in canonical time is quantized using the supplied timeline clock. With differing source rate the resulting raw source-frame index need not equal that same number of source-file seconds. The source datum and bytes remain unchanged; this mode must not be described as preserving pitch or the same physical source-time interval.

The active descriptor retains its accessor across blocks. Direct source-rate equality avoids rate-converter history. Each read copies the returned samples and applies checked Float32 event gain once. Rebase worker scheduling, UI seconds-to-start-frame and AVAudioEngine/device output remain application behavior, not a reconstructed full Cubase channel.

Picker labels project clock/unconverted, explains changed speed and pitch, states that Rebase supplies clock because original project rate is unrecovered, and retains separate original-rate and converter choices. Preparation creates ephemeral playback info; this diff does not rewrite saved CPR, attachment, frozen import timing or project clips.

Independent official Steinberg search results confirm unconverted differing-rate media can change speed/pitch, project sample rate governs recording/playback, and import conversion is a separate option. These pages do not specify exact frame quantization, endpoint behavior, effective native object state or current WAV backend.
